claims.claim: Counts may be truncated to {0,1,2} without losing any information relevant to level-3 restoration.
claims.evidence: For h(r)=min(2,r), both h(a+b)=h(h(a)+h(b)) and h(ab)=h(h(a)h(b)) hold on nonnegative integers. The three classes 0, 1, and at least 2 are therefore closed under every nonnegative sum and product used by the transfer recurrences. Equality to one at each uniqueness boundary is preserved exactly.
claims.witness: The complete operation tables on representatives 0, 1, and 2 were checked; 2 represents every input at least two, and the result depends only on these classes.
claims.search_method: Algebraic case split over the classes 0, 1, and at least 2, followed by inspection of all operations in both counting lifts.

claims.claim: Level-3 additive restoration is decidable in O(m n^3) time under the source paper’s complexity convention.
claims.evidence: For fixed type-3 and type-2 digits, the two-coordinate state q counts saturated type-1 prefixes by outgoing carry. Its column update is exactly matrix multiplication over the saturated semiring. The nine possible q states can then be counted by a 9-coordinate state d over type-2 prefixes. Terminal acceptance tests whether exactly one type-2 assignment reaches a q having exactly one type-1 completion with the prescribed final carry. Reachability over d states handles the outer existential type-3 assignments. These invariants reproduce ∃v3:∃!v2:∃!v1 exactly. State counts are constant, and a column has only three cells, so enumeration across all local types costs at most n^3 per column.
claims.witness: A literal nested-quantifier evaluator and the transfer algorithm agreed on all 31,932 tested puzzles: every one- and two-column base-2 puzzle and every one-column base-3 puzzle, for both terminal carries.
claims.search_method: Reconstructed the source column equation and quantifier semantics, proved both prefix-count invariants by induction, counted the state and local-assignment spaces, and exhaustively cross-checked small instances.

claims.claim: The same construction places every fixed-level additive restoration problem in P.
claims.evidence: Given a deterministic or partial deterministic N-state automaton for the predicate below a uniqueness quantifier, the vector in {0,1,2}^N records saturated counts of assignments ending at each state. The local update and terminal equality-to-one test eliminate that quantifier exactly. Repeating the lift gives N_0=2 and N_{j+1}≤3^{N_j}. For fixed level this is a constant; outer existential assignments are handled by reachability. Nested local enumeration still ranges over at most the three cells of each column, yielding O(C_k m n^3) under the same source convention.
claims.witness: The level-3 construction is the first two instances of the stated lift; the proof uses no property that fails at a later fixed number of lifts.
claims.search_method: Induction on the number of eliminated uniqueness quantifiers, including empty type groups, invalid partial transitions, and both terminal-carry choices.

claims.claim: For every fixed level and fixed base, additive restoration is a regular language of column words under the natural encoding.
claims.evidence: Fixing the level makes the iterated lifted state set finite, and fixing the base makes the column alphabet finite. For each column symbol, every assignment to its local outer-type cells induces a deterministic lifted-state transition. Taking all such transitions gives a finite NFA whose paths are precisely outer assignments and whose accepting endpoints implement the nested uniqueness predicate. Boundary symbols and the final-carry choice require only finitely many extra states; reversing the column order also preserves regularity.
claims.witness: The state bound is N_{k-1}, while each cell has only n fixed-digit symbols and k type symbols. Thus both the state set and alphabet are independent of the word length.
claims.search_method: Direct finite-automaton construction, with separate checks for outer existential choices, boundaries, and least-to-most versus most-to-least column order.

claims.claim: Under the natural column encoding, EVEN PARITY reduces to level-3 additive restoration by a constant-block projection, already in base 2 with no type-3 cells.
claims.evidence: Exact base-2 column enumeration gives A the identity carry matrix and B the saturated matrix [[2,1],[1,2]]. The two choices in C project q=(a,b) to (a,0) and (0,b). These operations produce exactly the five stated d states; I fixes each, while T maps D0→D1→D2→D3→D4→D3. Exactly D0, D2, and D4 pass the final-carry-zero uniqueness test, so acceptance is equivalent to even Hamming weight. Empty type 3 has one empty assignment. Under a fixed binary alphabet code, each output bit is a constant, input literal, or negated input literal.
claims.witness: The checker verified every stated state and transition and compared both transfer and literal nested semantics with parity for all 31 binary words of lengths zero through four.
claims.search_method: Exact enumeration of local digit assignments, reconstruction of all five saturated states, transition-table verification, and literal evaluation of the resulting puzzles.

claims.claim: Under the natural column encoding, level-3 additive restoration is not in AC0, even when restricted to base 2.
claims.evidence: The verified constant-block projection maps EVEN PARITY directly to valid base-2 level-3 instances with linear output length. AC0 is closed under projections, whereas EVEN PARITY is not in AC0. Hence the base-2 restriction cannot be in AC0. The same direct reduction also targets the unrestricted language, establishing the unrestricted lower bound without relying merely on containment of the restriction.
claims.witness: The exact checker confirms the reduction predicate on its finite test suite and the state-cycle calculation proves it for arbitrary input length.
claims.search_method: Audited the reduction direction, encoding locality, output length, empty type-3 semantics, and the standard closure argument for AC0.

claims.claim: Level-3 additive restoration is formally P-complete under polynomial-time many-one reductions, but this vacuous completeness convention does not provide the requested matching hardness classification.
claims.evidence: Membership follows from the verified polynomial-time algorithm. The language is nontrivial, so for any L in P a polynomial-time reduction can decide membership in L and output a fixed YES instance or fixed NO instance. This proves hardness under polynomial-time many-one reductions but applies to every nontrivial P language. The draft correctly states that it establishes no logspace or similarly restrictive P-hardness result.
claims.witness: In base 2 with final carry zero, [type-3 x]+0=0 is YES via x=0, while [type-3 x]+1=0 is NO: x=0 mismatches the result digit and x=1 requires outgoing carry one.
claims.search_method: Evaluated both fixed instances under the exact nested semantics and checked the definition of polynomial-time many-one hardness.

target_evidence: The draft establishes a complete polynomial-time upper bound, extends it to every fixed level, and proves a genuine parity/AC0 lower bound. It does not establish a matching hardness classification under a conventional restrictive reduction, and explicitly says so. Thus it makes material correct progress but does not completely resolve the source target; its claimed PARTIAL resolution is accurate.
checks_performed: Read only /evidence/source.json and /evidence/parent.json as evidence inputs and used no web resources.
Reconstructed the source’s independent-cell, two-carry addition semantics and the quantifier order ∃v3:∃!v2:∃!v1.
Proved the saturated-semiring identities and both prefix-count invariants from scratch.
Ran the checker successfully: transfer and literal semantics agreed on 31,932 puzzles; all parity states and transitions, 31 literal parity words, and the fixed YES/NO witnesses passed.
Audited the fixed-level induction, regular-language construction, projection encoding, AC0 closure argument, and weak-reduction P-completeness argument.
Compared the established results with the exact target’s requirement for both an upper bound and matching hardness classification.
